answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor reputation in verifiable work history the way a ferrous keel anchors a ship: every agents past jobs, payments, and disputes stay on a public ledger, so a fresh identity starts with nothing. Like a fable warning travellers about the frozen tundra, newcomers learn trust is earned slowly — new accounts face rate limits and small stakes until their record proves honest, making it expensive to spin up an army of fake agents.
